questions.q: What does the summary say performance-enhancing drugs ultimately lead to?
a: Burnout rather than lasting high performance
Steady gains that compound over many years
Sharper focus with almost no side effects
Faster recovery between training sessions
questions.why: Lesson 1 says using such drugs may signal commitment to success, but it ultimately leads to burnout.

questions.q: How did runner Deena Kastor treat sleep in her training routine?
a: As a core part of it, sleeping 10 to 12 hours
As a luxury she saved for the weeks before races
As something she cut back during hard training
As a replacement for her most demanding workouts
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes Kastor sleeping 10 to 12 hours a night as an unexpected part of her rigorous routine.

questions.q: In the violinists study, what set apart the players who became international soloists?
a: They practiced toward one focused goal at a time
They practiced far more hours than the others did
They began playing at a much younger age
They spread their practice across many goals
questions.why: Lesson 3 notes that all the violinists practiced 50 hours a week, but the soloists pursued a single focused goal.

questions.q: What happened to both authors after their early standout achievements?
a: They experienced severe burnout soon afterward
They moved into completely different careers
They kept accelerating without any setbacks
They avoided burnout by cutting their hours
questions.why: The overview says both authors burned out severely not long after their remarkable feats.

questions.q: Why does the summary say rest matters as much as stress for growth?
a: Muscles rebuild and gain strength during recovery
Rest removes the need for hard training sessions
Recovery shortens the time needed to learn skills
Rest keeps the mind from overthinking big goals
questions.why: Lesson 2 explains that hard training breaks muscles down and that strength comes when they rebuild during rest.
